sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the vote] The House voted 211-204 on Tuesday evening to refer Massie's impeachment resolution to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee, effectively killing the effort for the remainder of this Congress (Reuters, WSJ, Al Jazeera, USA Today, Reason, Military Times). Massie was the only Republican to vote against the motion; Rep. Kevin Kiley (I-CA) sided with Republicans. 11 Democrats and 7 Republicans did not vote. [VERIFIED FACT -- the charges] The eight articles accused Hegseth of waging the Iran war without congressional authorization, defying congressional withdrawal directives, extrajudicial killings of suspected drug traffickers in the Caribbean/Pacific, capturing Venezuela's president without a declaration of war, and retaliation against Sen. Mark Kelly. [VERIFIED FACT -- the revival] House Democrats are expected to revive the effort when they take control of Congress in January; Massie said he has no plan to reintroduce the articles himself but is 'quite certain' Democrats will pursue them. [VERIFIED FACT -- Trump's reaction] Trump posted on social media that the attempt 'miserably FAILED' and 'Every single Republican, except Thomas Massie, a major LOSER, voted in favor of Pete.' [VERIFIED FACT -- the context] Hegseth at his Nov 10 Pentagon press conference called the bid a 'farce' and likened it to Trump's two impeachments. Military Times: Democrats won 256 House seats to 168 Republicans and at least 54 Senate seats to 44 in the midterms.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct tiered publisher families: Reuters (T1 wire) + Wall Street Journal (T2) + Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA). USA Today, Reason, Military Times, SCMP, Newsmax, NY Post, The Sun have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration, though their tallies agree.
sections.what_disputed: The vote was procedural, not a vote on the articles themselves: referral to committee kills the effort for this Congress but is not an acquittal and not a vote on whether Hegseth should be impeached. Conviction in the Senate would require a two-thirds majority (67 votes) even if a Democratic House impeached in January -- with Democrats at 54 Senate seats (Military Times), removal would still need Republican votes. The 'Hegseth survives impeachment' framing in tabloid carriers overstates the outcome: he survives this Congress only. The narrow margin turned partly on absences (18 members absent). Speaker Johnson opposed the effort, calling impeachment 'in the middle of hostilities abroad' a bad look (recorded 2100-12).
sections.why_matters: 211 to 204. Congress just voted to kill the impeachment of the man running the Iran war -- one Republican broke ranks, 18 members didn't show up, and the Democrats who take over in January say they'll bring it right back. The war secretary survives -- for now.

totw_analysis: Our read: 211 to 204. Congress just voted to kill the impeachment of the man running the Iran war -- one Republican broke ranks, 18 members didn't show up, and the Democrats who take over in January say they'll bring it right back. The war secretary survives -- for now.
